Added 2026-08-15, eleven days before this gate existed, and it is not being brought up to the rule now. It is a real arming and it does run: measured 2026-08-27 in this worktree it plants a removed control delegation, a wrong row pin and a doctored SDK version among others, and reports `manifest selftest: 39 behaved, 0 did not` at exit 0. Two measurements keep it off the `control` list rather than an argument. (1) TIME: that run took 113.6s against this gate's CONTROL_TIMEOUT of 120s, so it clears by 6.4 seconds on an idle machine and would be reported as `control did not finish in 120s` — a rotted control — on a loaded one. A control whose verdict depends on machine load is the instrument this registry exists to distrust. (2) ENVIRONMENT: it reads the mcp method names out of the installed SDK and exits 2 with `environment: the MCP SDK is not installed. Run npm install.` without node_modules. Under `make lint` that is guaranteed by the `tools` target; run standalone, as the gate command in every brief here is, it is not. WHAT WOULD END THE GRANDFATHERING: either the selftest getting under the timeout with real headroom, or this gate growing a per-entry timeout so a slow control can declare its own cost — plus node_modules becoming a stated precondition of a standalone run rather than an accident of whether `make` went first.
